description_full: Eastman Chemical Company operates as a specialty materials company in the United States, China, and internationally. The company's Additives & Functional Products segment offers amine derivative-based building blocks, intermediates for surfactants, metam-based soil fumigants, and organic acid-based solutions; specialty coalescent and solvents, paint additives, and specialty polymers; and heat transfer and aviation fluids. It serves transportation, personal care, wellness, food, feed, agriculture, building and construction, water treatment, energy, consumables, durables, and electronics markets. Its Advanced Materials segment provides copolyesters, cellulosic biopolymers, polyvinyl butyral sheets, polyester films and window and protective films for value-added end uses in the transportation, durables, electronics, building and construction, medical and pharma, and consumables end-markets. The company's Chemical Intermediates segment offers olefin and acetyl derivatives, methylamines and salts, higher amines and solvents, ethylene, and commodity solvents; and primary non-phthalate and phthalate plasticizers, and niche non-phthalate plasticizers for industrial chemicals and processing, building and construction, health and wellness, and food and feed. Its Fibers segment provides cellulose acetate tow, triacetin, cellulose acetate flake, acetic acid, and acetic anhydride for use in filtration media primarily cigarette filters; natural and solution dyed acetate yarns, and staple fiber for use in consumables, and health and wellness markets; and wet-laid nonwoven media, specialty and engineered papers, and cellulose acetate fibers for transportation, industrial, agriculture and mining, and aerospace markets. Eastman Chemical Company was founded in 1920 and is headquartered in Kingsport, Tennessee.

financial_summary: Eastman Chemical Company is a mid-cap basic materials business with a $7.4B market cap on $8.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -6% over the past three years and -1% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 8% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 24% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $424M in free cash flow — roughly 5 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.05× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.9× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 2.6× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 5.2% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.5× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sector_headwinds.text: Low reinvestment-driven growth suggests the compounding engine has stalled
Fragmented industry with below-average profit capture — no moat to protect margins
Priced near or above estimated fair value, so the margin of safety has been bid away
Volatile returns on capital suggest the moat is narrower than a snapshot ROIC implies
Piotroski score 4/9 — below the median for a healthy business
Altman Z in the grey zone — financial health warrants monitoring
Above-average short interest at 7.3% of float
Carries more leverage than most Basic Materials peers — a smaller cushion for the inevitable bad year
Cyclical sectors like Basic Materials tend to underperform in slowdowns
Trade policy and tariff whiplash — materials producers are first-order casualties of protectionist swings, and margin gets squeezed from both input and output pricing.

sector_tailwinds: 32 consecutive years of dividend payments — an operating record that makes the dividend claim credible

sect: Its 6% operating margin is roughly in line with the Basic Materials median (10%).
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.50x its revenue share).
It accounts for 0.5% of sector revenue and 0.3% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-7.9% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.04 across 219 companies in the universe; the top four hold 25% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 13% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 9% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 23% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 32% and a beta of 1.07, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.44 vs 5y 1.09), so read it loosely.
About $78.4M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 50% in the 2020 crash, 43% in the 2022 bear market and 76% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $63.06 (margin of safety -2%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models corroborate one another (dispersion 6%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $44.64 to $88.13 (P10-P90).
On multiples it looks cheap against Basic Materials peers: P/E 11.5 vs 16.5 and P/FCF 17.4 vs 22.8 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 60% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 5.8% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 4.6% (vs the 8% bar).
The 16 covering analysts target $75.12 on average, 17% above the price.
prof: ROIC of 8% earns above the cost of capital of 8.0%, but the 0pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.51).
It runs a 24% gross margin and converts 5% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 2.05x.
ROE of 8% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (2.5x equity multiplier).
It spends 2.9% of revenue on R&D and 0.5% on stock compensation.
hlth: Leverage is heavy at 3.9x net debt to EBITDA ($566.0M of cash against $4.8B of debt), and interest cover is thin at 2.6x.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -6.1% over 3 years, 0.7% over 5 years and -1.0% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded -16.9% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.1x, 6.2% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 5, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 2.7% on average.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.9%), and institutions hold 95%.
It returns 5.2% a year to shareholders (5.2% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 32 consecutive years, raising it 1.3% a year over the last five.
people: With about 13,000 employees, each generates about $673K of revenue, in line with the Basic Materials median, and productivity has risen 2.7% a year.
That works out to $33K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.9M (4x revenue per employee).
